translationRepairs: Scholars are broadly learned, men of great talent and vessel; their ornamented prose shines and their brushwork weaves brocade; Yang Xiong cannot match their pens, Yu Xin cannot surpass their records; a letter flies and Liaocheng falls; pure talk rises and Ying's army retreats.

Scholars are broadly learned, men of great talent and vessel; their ornamented prose shines and their brushwork weaves brocade; Yang Xiong cannot match their pens, Yuanyu cannot surpass their records; a letter flies and Liaocheng falls; pure talk rises and Ying's army retreats.
子雲…元瑜 pairs Yang Xiong’s courtesy name with Ruan Yu’s courtesy name 元瑜; Yu Xin (庾信) is a later writer and is not in the Chinese.

Formerly Zengzi with broken ribs wandered in Qin and suddenly met Pan Cai; carrying matting he entered Zhao and at once was detained—today though I am a sojourner, compared with that it is not equal; the burden of Fan Lin—how could I bear it?

Formerly the man with broken ribs wandered in Qin and suddenly met favor; carrying a bamboo hat he entered Zhao and at once was detained—today though I am a sojourner, compared with that it is not equal; how could I bear such an undeserved favor?

The original invents Zengzi, Pan Cai, and Fan Lin as names; 折脅, 盼採, and 檐簦 are allusion phrases, not those persons. The proposal rightly removes them and renders 簦 as a bamboo hat, but 賁 is a gift or favor, not a “burden,” so the closing clause needs “undeserved favor.”
In the sixth year, his wife's elder brother Liu Xia used Jingli's power for repeated fraud and accepted one hundred bolts of silk from Ouyang Wuwei; Jingli was dismissed from office. [4]
In the sixth year, his wife's elder brother Liu Qia used Jingli's power for repeated fraud and accepted one hundred bolts of silk from Ouyang Wuwei; Jingli was dismissed from office. [4]
妻兄劉洽 has given name 洽 (qià); Liu Qia is the accurate romanization, and Liu Xia is not supported by the graph.
On "ji and Central Palace Attendants Zhu Tong, Yuan Shu, Zhang Zhong, Zhou Hongzheng, Hongrang, Shen Jiong, and Kong Huan": emended per all editions.
On "and the Central Palace Attendants Zhu Tong, Yuan Shu, Zhang Zhong, Zhou Hongzheng, Hongrang, Shen Jiong, and Kong Huan": emended according to all editions.

The collation restores 及 after rejecting 孔; 及 is the conjunction “and,” so bare “ji” wrongly looks like a name. The proposal’s sense is right, but the English field must not embed the Chinese graph—render plain “and.”
ji Central Palace Attendant Zhu Tong, Yuan Shu, Zhang Zhong, Zhou Hongzheng, Hongrang, Shen Jiong, and Kong Huan—changed according to all editions.
And Central Palace Attendant Zhu Tong, Yuan Shu, Zhang Zhong, Zhou Hongzheng, Hongrang, Shen Jiong, and Kong Huan—changed according to all editions.
Same lemma on the literal field: 及 is “and,” not a personal name “ji.” Keep that correction, but drop the parenthetical Chinese graph from the English replacement.

As men of letters they are broadly learned Confucians, men of outstanding talent and great vessel; their ornamented prose shines and their brushwork weaves brocade; Yang Xiong cannot match their pens, Yu Xin cannot surpass their records; a letter flies and Liaocheng falls; pure talk rises and Ying's army retreats.

As men of letters they are broadly learned Confucians, men of outstanding talent and great vessel; their ornamented prose shines and their brushwork weaves brocade; Yang Xiong cannot match their pens, Yuanyu cannot surpass their records; a letter flies and Liaocheng falls; pure talk rises and Ying's army retreats.

元瑜 is the courtesy name of Ruan Yu, not the later writer Yu Xin; that name error is real. The rest of the proposed rewrite is stylistic (通儒, 摛掞絢藻, 清談) and needlessly alters accurate wording; keep the human phrasing and only replace Yu Xin with Yuanyu.

Formerly Zengzi with broken ribs wandered in Qin and suddenly met Pan Cai; carrying matting he entered Zhao and at once was detained—today though I am a sojourner, compared with that it is not equal; the burden of Fan Lin—how could I bear it?

Formerly, a man whose ribs had been broken went to Qin and unexpectedly found favor; another entered Zhao carrying a long-handled rain hat and was promptly retained. Though I too am now a sojourner, I cannot compare with them; how could I be worthy of such favor?

折脅遊秦 and 檐簦入趙 allude to Fan Ju and Yu Qing without naming them; 盼採 means favor or selection, not a person Pan Cai; 簦 is a bamboo rain-hat, not matting; Zengzi and Fan Lin as named actors are invented. The proposed wording restores the unnamed allusions and sense of 樊林之賁 as favor.

In the sixth year, because his wife's elder brother Liu Xia had relied on Jingli's power to commit repeated frauds and had also accepted one hundred bolts of silk from Ouyang Wuwei, Jingli was dismissed from office.

In the sixth year, he was implicated when his wife's elder brother Liu Qia relied on Jingli's power and influence to commit repeated frauds and accepted a gift of one hundred bolts of silk from Ouyang Wuwei; Jingli was dismissed from office. [4]

劉洽 romanizes as Liu Qia, not Liu Xia; 坐 marks Jingli as implicated for his wife's elder brother's frauds, and the note marker [4] belongs in the English. The proposed literal restores the name, the 坐 construction, and the footnote.
